result.topic_en: Calculations with linear fractional (Möbius) transformations of the variable z: composing them, finding the two fixed points γ1, γ2, and reducing the transformation to a multiplication of the ratio (γ1 z+1)/(γ2 z+1).
result.transcription:
$\mathfrak{z} [-+-] \frac{\varrho^2}{\varrho_1^2}\mathfrak{z}$
$z \mp \frac{az+b}{cz+d}$
$\frac{\alpha z+\beta}{\gamma z+\delta} \mp \frac{\alpha(az+b)+\beta(cz+d)}{\gamma(az+b)+\delta(cz+d)}$
[-$\gamma a+\delta c = \gamma\varepsilon$-] $\gamma z+1 \mp \gamma(az+b)+cz+d$
[-$\gamma b+\delta d = \delta\varepsilon$-]
$a+\frac{c}{\gamma} = b\gamma+d$ $\gamma_1 \mid \gamma_2$
$\gamma_1 z+1 \mp$ [-$(\gamma\ldots)$-] $(b\gamma_1+d)(\gamma_1 z+1)$
$\gamma_2 z+1 \mp (b\gamma_2+d)(\gamma_2 z+1)$
$\frac{\gamma_1 z+1}{\gamma_2 z+1} = \mathfrak{z}.$
$\mathfrak{z} \mp \frac{b\gamma_1+d}{b\gamma_2+d}\mathfrak{z}$

methods.what: Scaling map of the variable by ratio of squared radii
Composition of a linear fractional function with a Möbius substitution
Condition (quadratic in γ) for γz+1 to transform into a multiple of itself, giving two roots γ1, γ2 (fixed points)
Eigen-forms γ_i z+1 transform by factor (bγ_i+d)
Normal form of a Möbius transformation: in the variable (γ1 z+1)/(γ2 z+1) it becomes multiplication by a constant
